newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania abandons plan for grain export bonuses.
newsitem.headline: Romania abandons plan for grain export bonuses.

text.p: Romania's government has abandoned a plan to offer bonuses to exporters of wheat and barley after running into opposition from international lenders, Agriculture Minister Dinu Gavrilescu said Friday.
"The government did not approve bonuses for exporters," Gavrilescu told a briefing during a cabinet meeting to discuss a long-awaited revised 1997 budget to meet IMF demands.

Gavrilescu said the World Bank and International Monetary Fund representatives, now reviewing Romania's reform progress, disagreed with the plan on grounds that it was not included in their loan accords and would increase spending.
An IMF team has been in Bucharest since mid-July to assess whether Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea's centrist government has met reform targets.
The Agriculture Ministry had planned bonuses of around 150 lei per kg for wheat and barley exporters to stimulate a new sowing campaign, Gavrilescu said.
"One reason for abandonding this was that such bonuses imply additional spending of 300 billion lei and we have to consider the budgetary restrictions we face," he said.
Gavrilescu said the government would stimulate exports by rescinding a 30 percent tax on wheat exports introduced this year to guard against domestic shortages before the harvest.
"That tax was valid until August 15 and we have abandoned it earlier than planned, from today," Gavrilescu said.

Romania expects a wheat harvest of around seven million tonnes, almost double last year's levels. So far the Balkan country has taken in about 56 percent of its wheat crop, as harvesting was dealyed by recent rains.
